SvelteKit passes a page only `data`, `form`, `params` and `snapshot`, a layout also `children`, and an error page `error`, under Svelte 5. Any other prop is always `undefined`. The rule checks `let { .. } = $props()` and, for Svelte 3 and 4, `export let`, where those may also take `errors`.

The rule looks only at components in the routes of a SvelteKit project: below `kit.files.routes` of `settings.svelte` or of the Svelte configuration, else below `src/routes`, in a project that has `@sveltejs/kit`.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/valid-prop-names-in-kit-pages": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"filename": "src/routes/+page.svelte", "packages": {"@sveltejs/kit": "2.5.0"}} */}

```svelte
<script>
  let { data, user } = $props();
</script>
```

Not reported:

{/* good {"filename": "src/routes/+page.svelte", "packages": {"@sveltejs/kit": "2.5.0"}} */}

```svelte
<script>
  let { data } = $props();
  let user = $derived(data.user);
</script>
```
